_strings.@@e56510847552: Treaty conformity — LA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from LA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the LA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: LA's resident return (IT-540) starts from Federal Adjusted Gross Income: Line 7 is "FEDERAL ADJUSTED GROSS INCOME" and the 2025 instructions say "Line 7 - Enter the amount of your Federal Adjusted Gross Income (Federal AGI). This amount is taken from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, Line 11. If your Federal AGI is less than zero, enter 0." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through. The only "additions" to federal AGI are on Schedule E; there is NO add-back of tax-treaty-exempt income anywhere on the IT-540 form, Schedule E, or in the 2025 instructions. Because LA starts from federal AGI and has no treaty addback, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> conforms. (Act 11's 2025 flat-rate reform did not change LA's federal-AGI starting point or add any treaty addback.)

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: IT-540 Line 11: 'YOUR LOUISIANA INCOME TAX'. 2025 instructions, Line 11: 'Multiply Line 10 by .03. Round to the nearest dollar.' Line 10 = Line 7 Federal Adjusted Gross Income minus Line 8 standard deduction ($12,500 filing status 1/3; $25,000 filing status 2/4/5) minus Line 9D excess federal itemized deductions, floor zero ('Subtract Lines 8 and 9D from Line 7. If less than zero, enter zero 0'). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 STRUCTURAL CHANGE (Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Legislative Session): Louisiana went FLAT. The graduated 1.85%/3.5%/4.25% brackets and the combined personal exemption-standard-deduction zero-rate floor of 2023/2024 are GONE. For tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2025 the rate is a FLAT 3% (IT-540 Line 11 = Line 10 x .03). Do NOT use this pack for 2024 or earlier, and do NOT carry 2024 graduated figures into 2025. Base guidance: supply IT-540 Line 10 as taxable_base -> the op recomputes it here as Line 7 Federal AGI minus the per-status Line 8 standard deduction, so supply Line 7 FEDERAL ADJUSTED GROSS INCOME (Federal Form 1040/1040-SR, Line 11; if less than zero enter 0; if you have Louisiana additions/exempt income, Line 7 comes from Louisiana Schedule E instead) as taxable_base and the op subtracts the standard deduction. IMPORTANT: if you are a FEDERAL ITEMIZER you must also subtract Line 9D 'EXCESS FEDERAL ITEMIZED DEDUCTIONS' yourself before supplying the base (this op models only the standard deduction, not Line 9D). Non-itemizers skip Lines 9A-9D. Standard deduction (Line 8, Act 11): $12,500 for filing status 1 (single) or 3 (married filing separately); $25,000 for filing status 2 (married filing jointly), 4 (head of household), or 5 (qualifying surviving spouse) - nearly tripled from the 2024 $4,500/$9,000 combined floors. The op's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping is exact ($25,000). Head of Household ALSO gets $25,000 for 2025 (up from the old $9,000 combined floor and no longer sharing the single boundary) - the shipped head_of_household amount reflects this. The standard deduction is CPI-U indexed annually starting after 2025; these are the 2025 amounts. Exemptions REPEALED: Act 11 repealed the additional $1,000 deductions for dependents, persons 65 or older, and blind persons (old Lines 6A/6B/6D/6E/6F), and those lines were removed from the 2025 form. This pack ships NO exemption keys - pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0. (The prior graduated packs' 'dependent'/'age_65'/'blind' $1,000 entries do not exist for 2025.) No tax table: 2025 Line 11 is a straight multiplication printed on the form ('Multiply Line 10 by .03. Round to the nearest dollar') - the 2024 Louisiana Tax Table no longer applies. This op's irs_round matches the form's round-to-nearest-dollar. Louisiana credits are NOT modeled by this op and come off after Line 11: Nonrefundable Priority 1 credits (Schedule C) on Line 12; refundable child care credit (federal AGI <= $25,000) on Line 14; refundable school readiness credit (star-rated) on Line 15; Louisiana Earned Income Credit (5% of the federal EIC) on Line 16; other refundable Priority 2/4 and nonrefundable Priority 3 credits (Schedules F/I/J) on later lines. Annual Retirement Income Exemption for taxpayers 65 or older (Schedule E Code 06E) increased from $6,000 to $12,000 per person for 2025 (Act 11) - this is a Schedule E base subtraction reached on Line 7, not part of this Line 11 computation; supply Line 7 already net of any Schedule E exemptions. Consumer Use Tax (Line 23A) and the Electric/Hybrid Vehicle Road Usage Fee are separate amounts added on the 2025 return after the income tax - NOT modeled. Source URL: 2025 resident instructions https://dam.ldr.la.gov/taxforms/IT540i-WEB-2025.pdf ; reform bulletin https://dam.ldr.la.gov/lawspolicies/RIB-25-012-Louisiana-Individual-Income-Tax-Reform-1.pdf .
